title: Periodicity, fundamental period, and trigonometric domains and ranges
section: Trigonometry ▷ Periodicity and Graphs of the Trig Functions
terms: periodic function; period; fundamental period; amplitude; phase shift; trigonometric asymptote.

exposition.text:
A positive number T is a period when translation by T preserves the domain and f (x + T ) =
f(x) throughout it. If a smallest positive period exists, it is the fundamental period. Sine and
cosine have fundamental period 2π; tangent and cotangent have period π. A constant has every
positive period and no smallest one. For nonzero b, replacing x by bx divides a fundamental
period by |b|.
Sine and cosine have domain R and range [−1, 1]. Tangent and secant exclude π/2 + kπ; cotan-
gent and cosecant exclude kπ. Tangent and cotangent have range R, while secant and cosecant
have range (−∞, −1] ∪ [1, ∞). In A sin(bx + c) + d, |A| is amplitude, −c/b the horizontal phase
shift, and d the midline.
The excluded inputs of tangent, secant, cotangent, and cosecant are vertical asymptotes: the
function becomes unbounded on approach from at least one side. Phase shifts translate these
asymptotes; a nonzero vertical scale does not remove them.

question.text:
What is the smallest positive period of f(x) = sin(2x) + cos(3x)?
(A) π/3 (B) π/2 (C) π (D) 2π (E) 6π

solution.text:
The frequencies 2 and 3 must each acquire phase an integer multiple of 2π under a pe-
riod; this follows from linear independence of the distinct exponential frequencies. Thus
2T, 3T ∈ 2πZ, and their common smallest positive solution is T = 2π.

question.text:
How many points in [0, 2π) are excluded from the natural domain of tan(2x) + csc(3x)?
(A) 6 (B) 8 (C) 9 (D) 10 (E) 12

solution.text:
Tangent excludes x = π/4, 3π/4, 5π/4, 7π/4, four points. Cosecant excludes x = kπ/3 for
k = 0, . . . , 5, six points. None coincide: (2j + 1)π/4 = kπ/3 would give 3(2j + 1) = 4k,
impossible by parity. Thus ten points are excluded.

question.text:
The function f(x) = 3 − 2 sin(4x − π/3) first attains its maximum at a positive x = a. What is a?
(A) π/24 (B) π/12 (C) 5π/24 (D) 11π/24 (E) 7π/12

solution.text:
The maximum is 5, attained when sin(4x − π/3) = −1. Thus 4x − π/3 = −π/2 + 2kπ, giving
x = −π/24 + kπ/2. The smallest positive value corresponds to k = 1 and equals 11π/24.

question.text:
For g(x) = 2 sec x − 3, which pair gives its range and all its vertical asymptotes?
(A) (−∞, −5] ∪ [−1, ∞); x = π/2 + kπ (B) [−1, ∞); x = kπ
(C) (−∞, −1] ∪ [1, ∞); x = π/2 + kπ (D) (−∞, −5] ∪ [−1, ∞); x = kπ
(E) R; x = π/2 + kπ

solution.text:
The secant range is (−∞, −1] ∪[1, ∞). Multiplying by 2 and subtracting 3 yields (−∞, −5] ∪
[−1, ∞). Poles occur where cos x = 0, namely x = π/2+kπ, and these remain vertical asymp-
totes after the affine output change.
